title: Chronic Catheterization of Carotid Artery and Jugular Vein in Mice
author: Bingle Bracy
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zddf226
materials: Blunt dissect to expose right jugular vein.
The bead must lie flat around the catheter.

steps.title: Prepare Arterial Catheters
steps.instruction: Construct the arterial catheters using PE-10 and silastic tubing.

substeps.instruction: Cut 10 cm of PE-10 and stretch the tubing to approximately 13 cm.
Cut the stretched PE-10 into 1.3 cm pieces.
Cut silastic tubing (0.012” ID) into 6 cm pieces.
Insert Dumont forceps into the end of a 6 cm silastic piece and gently open them to widen the tubing.
Grasp a stretched 1.3 cm PE-10 piece with Graefe forceps and insert the tip into the silastic tubing by approximately 3 mm.
Remove the Dumont forceps, leaving the PE-10 in place.

steps.title: Prepare Venous Catheters
steps.instruction: Construct the venous catheters using silastic tubing and a restraining bead.

substeps.instruction: Cut a 6 cm piece of silastic tubing (0.012” ID).
Cut a 1 mm section of silastic tubing (0.020” ID) to serve as a restraining bead.
Insert eye dressing forceps into the lumen of the bead and gently hold the tips apart to stretch the opening.
Using another pair of eye dressing forceps, slide the 6 cm silastic tubing into the lumen of the bead.
Pull the silastic tubing through the bead until it reaches 11 mm, ensuring the bead lies flat around the catheter.

steps.title: Prepare MASA tm Rig
steps.instruction: Assemble the MASA tm device using stainless steel and PE-20 tubing.

substeps.instruction: Cut two 1.3 cm long stainless steel tubes using a file and smooth the edges with an abrasive stone.
Cut two 2.5 cm long PE-20 pieces and attach #2 to #1.
Bend each stainless steel tube in half at a 120° angle.
Slide silastic tubing (0.058” ID) over the junction where both stainless steel tubes and PE-20 are attached.
Place the completed rig in silicone medical adhesive for 24 hours.
Cut catheter plugs from steel wire for use during surgery.

steps.title: Pre-Surgical Animal Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the mouse and the surgical environment for asepsis.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse.
Bevel catheters to correct lengths, fill with 200U heparinized saline, and plug.
Remove hair from the surgical site in an area separate from the surgery site.
Disinfect the surgical sites using Nolvasan followed by alcohol in a disinfected area.
Administer Ketoprofen (5-10 mg/kg) subcutaneously.
Wash and dry hands, then aseptically don sterile surgical gloves.

steps.title: Insert Arterial Catheter
steps.instruction: Perform surgery to place the catheter in the left carotid artery.

substeps.instruction: Make a small vertical midline incision 5 mm cephalic to the xiphoid process.
Blunt dissect with forceps to expose and reflect the left sternomastoid muscle to expose the left carotid artery.
Tease off connective tissue, isolating the vagus nerve from the artery without damaging either.
Ligate the cephalic end of the artery with silk suture and place a loose knot on the caudal end.
Clamp the vessel with a micro-serrefine and cut just below the ligated end with spring scissors.
Insert the catheter as far as possible, then release the micro-serrefine clamp and continue inserting to the silastic-polyethylene junction (tip should be in the aortic arch).
Tie both ligatures securely, confirm the catheter samples, and flush with heparinized saline.

steps.title: Insert Venous Catheter
steps.instruction: Perform surgery to place the catheter in the right jugular vein.

substeps.instruction: Make an incision 5 mm to the right of the midline and approximately 2 mm caudal to the first incision.
Blunt dissect to expose the right jugular vein.
Isolate the vein and ligate the cephalic end with silk suture; loosely tie another suture at the caudal end.
Cut just below the cephalic ligature with spring scissors.
Insert the catheter to the bead, tie, confirm it samples, and flush with heparinized saline.

steps.title: Exteriorize Catheters and Close
steps.instruction: Tunnel the catheters to the back and secure them to the MASA tm rig.

substeps.instruction: Turn the mouse over and make a small incision between the shoulder blades.
Tunnel a 14-gauge needle under the skin through the dorsal incision.
Thread both catheters through the needle to exteriorize them to the back.
Close the ventral incisions with nylon suture.
Clamp the venous catheter with a micro-serrefine at the dorsal incision site, cut 1 cm above the clamp, and connect to the MASA tm.
Ensure no holes or kinks exist and secure the venous catheter to the MASA tm with silk suture; repeat for the arterial catheter.
Close the dorsal incision with nylon, confirm patency of both catheters again, and flush with heparinized saline.
Place the mouse in a warmed, clean cage.
